grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: 12 to 13 minutes gives a fully hard-boiled egg
grounding.from: Healthline says 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs that are not over-cooked.

grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: 10 minutes is mostly cooked but slightly soft in the center
grounding.from: At 10 minutes, the eggs are mostly cooked through but slightly soft in the center.

grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: 15 minutes gives rubbery whites and powdery dry yolks
grounding.from: RecipeTin Eats (about 12 days old) says 10 minutes is classic hard boiled, and 15 minutes gives rubbery whites and powdery dry yolks.

grounding.states: smaller eggs cook quicker than large ones
grounding.from: Healthline says these times are for large eggs: smaller ones cook quicker while larger ones need extra time.

value.answer: For large eggs dropped into boiling water, 12 to 13 minutes gets a fully set yolk. 10 minutes is firm but a bit soft in the middle. Go much past 14 or 15 and the whites go rubbery and the yolk dry and powdery. Smaller eggs need a little less time.
